title: Allow research task selection from sparse checkouts
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The task picker currently rejects a sparse checkout when any card's first-step script, starting point or priority log is absent, even if that card is unrelated to the requested task. It now accepts an absent reference only when it is a regular file in HEAD and has a matching, stage-zero skip-worktree index blob. Sparse omissions are explicitly listed in the JSON receipt; the seed, track, methods and scope keys are unchanged.

This is a tooling repair. It validates catalogue references, not replay dependencies; users must materialize their chosen task's inputs before execution. Scientific sources, allocations, selected records and source pins are unchanged. No supplier admission or new kappa is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Base and refreshed canonical main: `18aacb215fc3717b06be8ceb9fca62aeca0d3e99`, priority revision 6.
- Task/scope: `portable-replay` / `chooser-sparse-catalogue-regular-head-files`; **changed scope** from the `adversarial-audit` draw, nonce `6c43ccec08828911d1cc13913048461f`.
- The live check showed the inspected scatter and corrected-census follow-ups already covered by #2992/#3004/#3100 and #3005. Those retain their results and credit. This change instead fixes the independently reproduced onboarding failure encountered while using a sparse checkout after disk exhaustion.
- Domain and stop rule: catalogue path availability and task-selection receipts only, using real temporary Git repositories. No scientific replay provisioning or catalogue reallocation.
- [Canonical scope/coordination](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200#discussioncomment-18985902). Final overlap at 2026-10-17 00:45 UTC covered 253 open PRs and 1,861 discussion/comment/reply records, complete pagination and no warnings. Sparse local-note coverage and no code-diff search remain limits. No competing chooser fix was found.

## Validation

Passed locally on macOS arm64, Git 2.53.0, CPython 3.12.14:

```sh
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_assignment.py' -v
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_coordination.py'
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_onboarding.py'
git diff --check
```

All **50 tests pass without skips** (16 assignment, 8 coordination, 26 onboarding). New controls cover non-cone sparse checkout, cone sparse index, unchanged full/sparse CLI receipts, ordinary deletions, unknown paths, staged replacements, staged-only entries, omitted symlink entries, directory/external alias substitutions and Git failure. An original-source comparison rejects the same sparse fixture that the changed helper accepts. Existing full-checkout behavior remains available without Git path lookup when all references are present.

The actual sparse checkout also successfully runs:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/choose_research_task.py --seed 6c43ccec08828911d1cc13913048461f
```

It reports 34 omitted catalogue paths and retains all three original adversarial-audit scope keys and the unchanged selected-record SHA256 `bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129`. The assignment tests also passed on CPython 3.14.7 before the final added cone-index control; the full 50-test result above is the canonical Python 3.12 run. Hosted CI, Windows execution and the selected mathematical cold replay are not claimed.

## Credit and remaining work

Credit Douglas Colkitt and the repository onboarding contributors for the picker and standing procedure. Arham Tahir prepared this focused fix with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. This is author-checked, not independent human review.

Scientific dependency hydration remains a separate task; the new receipt explicitly says the catalogue check cannot establish replay readiness. No additional research package or mathematical obligation is introduced. [Workflow feedback and scope-change rationale](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200#discussioncomment-18985902).
